uncertain.text: auoit deux ſoubredens à la machoire de
uncertain.note: a small raised ink mark stands between 'machoire' and 'de' (pages/strips/p061/body-4.jpg, last line, x~1480-1520; checked at 10x). It sits at the top of the x-height like a marker letter, but it is an unformed blob with no identifiable letter shape and there is a second speck below the baseline under it. NOT transcribed as a marker, because (a) no margin note anywhere on the page could key to it (only f and g are printed, both beside the first paragraph, and margin-2/3/4 are blank), and (b) no TEXTE block in any finished page of this edition carries a marker. Most likely offset or a stray sort. If the reconciler decides it is a marker, the key would be 'h' and the note is missing.

uncertain.text: Ceci me faict ſouuenir de Q Fabius Maximus, le
uncertain.note: no point is printed after the praenomen abbreviation Q: at 7x the sort is a capital Q with a long flat tail, followed by a wide blank and then 'Fabius'. Transcribed 'Q Fabius' as printed; the expected 'Q.' would need a dot that is simply not on the page (the tail runs at baseline level, well left of where a point would sit).

sic: the surname is set 'Rols' here (third letter a full-height l with no dot, checked at 4x) but 'Rois' five lines down in 'qui eſpouſa ladite de Rois' (short dotted i, same zoom). Both transcribed as printed; the variation is the compositor's, not a misreading.

the last word is read 'fut.' — f, u, then the curl-topped italic t (same sort as the t of 'penulti-' two lines above), checked at 9x. The expected law-title abbreviation would be 'de fur.' (de furtis), so a reader may be tempted to write r; the printed sort is a t.
